importantFindings.title: Wildcard: when a 0.3.0 tab opens the database while the 0.4.0 app is still open, its schema drops dutySettingItems. 'Elimina il corso' in the 0.4.0 app then fails every time until a reload. At d19b51b the same erase ran in the same state.
importantFindings.evidence: eraseAllCourseData (src/persistence/courses.ts:77-84) runs DELETE on every COURSE_DATA_TABLES entry, which now includes dutySettingItems (src/persistence/schema.ts:176), inside one write transaction. Opening the 0.3.0 schema removes the table (ps_data_local__dutySettingItems is absent from sqlite_master), so the transaction fails with 'no such table: dutySettingItems'. Results on the real engine at 1a86168, clean tree (runs finished before the working-tree edits of 18:52). (1) Chromium UI (probe B): the app is open on the 0.3.0 fixture and a second page opens the 0.3.0 schema. Impostazioni > 'Elimina il corso e inizia un nuovo corso' > tick > 'Elimina tutto' shows 'Il corso non è stato eliminato. Nessun dato è cambiato: riprova.' 'Crea il corso' is not shown, and all 7 students remain. (2) Same page on both engines (probe D): Chromium and WebKit each give {itemsTablePresent:false, baseline:'Error: rollback-probe: every DELETE ran', erase:'Error: no such table: dutySettingItems', students:7}. The baseline probe runs d19b51b's statement list (COURSE_TABLES without dutySettingItems, reversed) in a transaction that is then rolled back, so before D2 the erase would have completed. Retrying in the same page meets the same missing table; only a reload re-creates it. Nothing is half-written and the message is accurate. In this state D1 already makes stamped writes fail (D1 DI-R2-Q5), and at d19b51b the new course created after the erase would also have failed. The privacy action (erasing minors' data), however, worked before D2 and does not now. This is the checklist's own case ('a 0.3.0 app opening the database, which drops the new table') with the newer instance still open. Neither D3 nor D4 lists it: D3 names Riprova of prepareDatabase, and D4 names a reset with another tab open, not an erase after an older schema dropped a newer table.

importantFindings.title: Independent reproduction of data-integrity DI-R2-1: at 1a86168, a duty-setting row whose columns disagree with its id makes the open-time repair or the duty save insert an id that already exists
importantFindings.evidence: Real SQLite (node:sqlite), running 1a86168's repairs.ts and dutyItems.ts (git show copies). Row W1: an unparsable stay-over list plus a completed-day row rewritten to kind 'stay-over'. The per-list skip filters stored rows by their columns (repairs.ts:143-147), the diff keys them by id, and repairDutySettingItems throws 'UNIQUE constraint failed: dutySettingItems.id'. On the real engine that rejects prepareDatabase on every open. Row W3: a row carrying this course's item id under another courseId. saveDutyPlan's item step reads only `WHERE courseId = ?` (duties.ts:293-298) and throws the same error, so every duty save fails ('Modifica non salvata') until the next open. Row W3b: the next open's repair then heals it. d19b51b had neither failure mode. Only 0.4.0 writes these rows, always consistent with their ids, so a corrupted database is needed to reach this. The consequence for W1 is the same total lockout I rated important in DP-3. The working tree (uncommitted, 18:52) changes both statements; that change was not reviewed here.

Run: npx vitest run -c test-results/d2-r2-pm/unit/vitest.config.ts. Result: W1 and W3 fail with UNIQUE constraint; W3b, W4, W5, W6 and W8 pass.
